speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have had these skin lesions, and do they itch or hurt?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the presence of similar lesions in daycare and the recent chickenpox in your brother are very telling. Has the child had any fever, runny nose, or general feeling of being unwell alongside these spots? Please also tell me if the lesions look like blisters or if they are firm bumps.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic, and the daycare exposure supports a viral transmission, even though the patient is up-to-date on chickenpox immunizations.
